article.dek: A nor'easter is parked over MetLife and the app's Hit Rate card, Saturday's roster moves are in, and Monday night's quarterback picture just got murky again.

items.headline: A nor'easter is parked on top of the app's Hit Rate card
paragraphs: Titans at Giants, 1 p.m. ET Sunday at MetLife: rain through the whole game, low 60s, north wind around 18 mph with gusts as high as 41 mph, and a 90% chance of precipitation, per the National Weather Service. It is the ugliest weather game on the board by a mile.

Here is why it leads the brief: the app's Hit Rate card tonight is Giants moneyline at -135 on DraftKings. That is the same game, the same storm. The app's model says the Giants win about 73 times in 100; the -135 price implies about 56. The app grades this one LOW confidence and prices it at negative expected value - and its own tutorial says 'Hit Rate is not Profit Rate.' The card's job is 'which supported pick looks most likely to win,' not 'which bet makes money.'

The weather does not change the app's number. It changes how the game is played - wet ball, kicking adventure, running game. And the app already drew your line in the sand: Play Through -137. One book is already showing -140 on the Giants. Past -137, the app's own guidance says stop chasing it there.

sources.label: The Spun (NWS forecast via Jim Wyatt)

items.takeaway: The storm is real, the card is real, and the play-through number is the line between them.

bullets: Bears: Caleb Williams (hamstring) is OUT for Monday night. But the quarterback picture just got murky again - Tyson Bagent practiced fully Saturday and is listed questionable. He needs two straight symptom-free days to clear concussion protocol. The app still shows Case Keenum as the expected starter, because its board is from this morning and has not seen this news yet.

Eagles: good news and bad news for Monday night. Saquon Barkley (stinger) and DeVonta Smith (hamstring) both practiced fully Saturday and will play. Out: receiver Hollywood Brown (ankle), tight end Dallas Goedert (knee), and tackle Fred Johnson (knee). Linebacker Jonathan Greenard (pec) practiced fully but is questionable.

Broncos: running back Jonah Coleman (ankle) went on injured reserve Saturday - out at least four games. That is ahead of Sunday night against the Rams, with RJ Harvey and J.K. Dobbins carrying the backfield.

Chargers: lineman Trey Pipkins III (knee) went on injured reserve Saturday. Backup quarterback Trey Lance is questionable, so the team signed DJ Uiagalelei to the active roster. Tight end Patrick Herbert and linebacker Caleb Murphy were elevated with David Njoku and Charlie Kolar hurt - ahead of Sunday at Buffalo.
49ers: receiver Demarcus Robinson (ankle) went on injured reserve Saturday - out at least four games, ahead of Sunday's home game against Arizona.

Still standing from Friday: Sam Darnold is cleared and starts for Seattle; the Ravens are without left tackle Ronnie Stanley in Rio with rookie Carson Vinson making his first start; Zay Flowers (hamstring) is a game-time call; Jameis Winston starts for the Giants with Jaxson Dart on injured reserve.
items.headline: Saturday's injury and roster news, all in one place
paragraphs: Everything that changed today, grouped together. Nothing scattered anywhere else in this brief.
items.takeaway: The Monday-night quarterback is the one to watch. Everything else is depth-chart damage, priced or priceable.

items.headline: Weather everywhere else: one more game to note
paragraphs: Seahawks at Commanders in Landover (1 p.m. ET) is the only other game on the radar: a 43-44% chance of light rain and northwest wind building to 15 mph, mid-60s. Worth knowing, not worth building around.

The rest is clean. Rio is overcast but dry at 71 for the Ravens and Cowboys. Sunday night in Denver is 82 and mostly cloudy. Buffalo, Cleveland, Cincinnati, Tampa, Jacksonville, Miami and Santa Clara all check out fine.
items.takeaway: Two games have weather. One of them has a nor'easter.

items.headline: What the three cards actually say tonight
paragraphs: The board has not refreshed since this morning, so the cards are the same three. Here is each one in plain language, with the price explained as price - not as a betting slip.

Balanced: Vikings moneyline at -120 on DraftKings. The -120 means every $1.20 you risk wins $1. The model says Minnesota wins about 59 times in 100; the price implies about 53. Small gap, medium confidence, 0.75 units. Balanced is the 'strong pick without paying too much' card - the middle ground, and the app's own words call it a good starting point for a new bettor. It is not supposed to be the +EV play. It is doing its job.

Hit Rate: Giants moneyline at -135 on DraftKings. The -135 means every $1.35 you risk wins $1. The model says the Giants win about 73 times in 100; the price implies about 56 - the biggest model-vs-price gap on the board. But the app grades it LOW confidence and negative expected value. Hit Rate asks 'which supported pick looks most likely to win,' and the tutorial literally says 'Hit Rate is not Profit Rate.' The low grade is the app telling you the number is loud but shaky - in a nor'easter, no less. That is information, not a defect.

Value: Raiders +3 at +102 on DraftKings. The +102 means every $1 you risk wins $1.02 if Las Vegas stays within a field goal or wins outright. The model says that happens about 50 or 51 times in 100; the price implies about 47. This is the only one of the three the app prices as positive expected value (+3.6%), medium confidence, 0.75 units. Value is always the model's +EV play. That is its whole job.

For your actual stake, the app does the math for you - it uses your bankroll and your staking setting, and it is deliberately conservative. The unit numbers above are the app's sizing language, not a dollar instruction.
items.takeaway: Three cards, three different questions. Read the question each one is answering before you read the pick.

items.headline: How to use the storm news with the app
paragraphs: News first, app second. The nor'easter is real news. Here is how to actually use it.

The weather does not rewrite the app's number - the model priced the teams, not the clouds. What weather CAN do is move the market: if bettors pile onto a side because of the storm, the price moves, and the price is what you pay. So the move to watch is the Giants' price, not the rain gauge.

The app already gave you the tripwire: Play Through -137 on the Giants card. The morning board had -135. Saturday afternoon, one book showed -140. At -140 you are past the app's own line - the price has eaten the idea at the app's number. That does not mean the Giants cannot win. It means the app's guidance at that price is: don't chase.

And if your book is not DraftKings or FanDuel, or it shows a different number than the app's board, you do not have to guess. Tap Check in the app, type in YOUR book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator and gives you a bet-or-no-bet verdict on your price. It is a full re-evaluation of your number, not a blind override of the board.
items.takeaway: The app's number is the anchor. The play-through is the tripwire. Check is how you price your own book.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Saturday's board: what moved, what didn't
paragraphs: Every line move in this brief lives in this section. Here is the Saturday delta against the morning board.

Titans at Giants: no move. The morning board had Giants -2.5 with a 37.5 total. Saturday afternoon it is still Giants -2.5 and still 37.5. A full day of nor'easter headlines moved the spread and total nowhere - the storm was priced in early. The only flicker is the moneyline price: -135 in the morning, -140 at one book Saturday afternoon. The line did not move; the fee got a little thicker.

Chiefs at Dolphins: the week's drift has parked. Kansas City opened the week -11.5, drifted to -10 / -10.5 by Friday, and sits at -10.5 with a 45 total Saturday afternoon. Quiet all day. The app's model has never been close to this number - it sees Kansas City by about 4 - and nothing Saturday changed that disagreement.

Ravens at Cowboys in Rio: still Baltimore -3.5. The Stanley and Flowers news has had more than 24 hours to get priced, and the market has not blinked. The app's model still disagrees by about five points (it sees Dallas by 1.5). A gap that wide in a weird stadium is a reason to study, not a reason to bet.

One structural note: the app's board refreshes twice a day, and the board you are reading is the morning one. Anything that moves tonight - the Seattle safeties news from Friday night is still the candidate - will not show up until the next refresh. And the real Monday-night wildcard is the Bears' quarterback: if Bagent clears protocol Sunday, that number moves before the app's next board does. That is exactly the spot the Check tab exists for - type in your book's fresh line and price and get the verdict on your number, not yesterday's.
items.takeaway: Saturday was a holding day. The next moves come from Sunday inactives and the Bears' quarterback.

items.headline: Sunday morning, in this order
paragraphs: Three live things to re-check before the early games: the final MetLife forecast (rain timing decides how ugly that game gets), whether Seattle's line drifts on the safeties news, and the inactive lists 90 minutes before kickoff - Zay Flowers is the game-time call that matters. If you like a number tonight, write it down, then compare it to Sunday's price before you do anything. The best bet is often the same bet at a better price.

sources.label: The Spun (NWS forecast via Jim Wyatt)

items.takeaway: Tonight's prices are a snapshot. Sunday morning's are the decision.

items.headline: Betting term of the day: juice
paragraphs: Juice is the fee baked into the price. At -110, you risk $1.10 to win $1 - that extra ten cents is the book's cut. At -120, you risk $1.20 to win the same $1 - twenty cents of fee for the identical win chance. Same pick, more juice, worse price.

That is what the app's Play Through number is actually telling you. Play Through -137 on the Giants means: up to -137, the fee is tolerable for the idea; past it, the juice ate the idea. When you see a price drifting - like the Giants ticking from -135 toward -140 - you are watching the juice get thicker in real time.
items.takeaway: The pick is the idea. The juice is what you pay for it. Never pay more juice than the idea is worth.

items.headline: Log the losers too
paragraphs: Settlement in the app is manual - there is no auto-settle yet, so wins and losses only exist if you record them. The tracker only works if you are honest with yourself, and honesty includes the ugly ones. A tracker with only wins is a highlight reel, not a record.
items.takeaway: The log is the discipline. Keep it complete.
